 FDA announces recall of more than 4.3 million tubes of fluoride toothpaste
 By Chris Williams FOX Local Health Published  October 21, 2026 1:35 PM EDT Share
 Copy Link 
 Email 
 Facebook 
 Twitter 
 LinkedIn 
 Reddit 
 Published  October 21, 2026 1:35 PM EDT article Toothbrush with toothpaste and tube on white towel, closeup 
 The Brief
 The FDA announced a voluntary nationwide recall of more than 4.3 million tubes of fluoride toothpaste. 
 The recalled products were sold under brands including Brush Buddies, Crayola, Hot Wheels, My Little Pony, evo, ARU and BB. 
 The recall involves multiple flavors, sizes and expiration dates and was initiated because of current good manufacturing practice deviations. 
 The Food and Drug Administration announced the recall of more than 4.3 million tubes of fluoride toothpaste distributed nationwide because of current good manufacturing practice deviations.
 Dig deeper:
 The voluntary recall was initiated by Pritam International Private Limited, an India-based manufacturer, on Sept. 10. The FDA classified the recall as Class II on Oct. 19.
 The recalled products include toothpaste sold under the Brush Buddies, Crayola, Hot Wheels, My Little Pony, evo, ARU and BB brands. The products include anticavity fluoride toothpastes in flavors such as bubble gum, strawberry, watermelon, peppermint, sweet mint, cool mint and various ice cream flavors.
 Popcorn stuck in man's teeth leads to life-threatening infection 
 FROM THE ARCHIVES: A British firefighter, 41, developed a life-threatening infection and underwent open-heart surgery after using items to dislodge a piece of popcorn stuck in his teeth.
 RELATED: FDA recalls GLP-1 drug, other injectable medication over sterility concerns 
 The products were distributed by Ashtel Studios Inc., based in Ontario, California. The recalled toothpaste comes in 3.5-ounce and 4-ounce tubes, as well as a two-pack containing two 3.5-ounce tubes.
 The recall includes products with expiration dates ranging from November 2026 through June 2028. Consumers should check the lot numbers and expiration dates listed on the FDA’s recall notice to determine whether they have an affected product.
 The FDA notice did not report any illnesses or injuries linked to the recalled toothpaste. 
 What you can do:
 Consumers who have recalled products should stop using them and contact the retailer or manufacturer for information about returns or refunds.
 The Source: The information in this story came from a recall notice issued by the Food and Drug Administration. This story was reported from Los Angeles.
